Buy Tickets We are proud to debut “Princess Diana: Love Life Legacy — A Life of Giving,” marking the exhibition's first stop anywhere in the world. This remarkable exhibition showcases more than 700 original artifacts spanning every chapter of Diana's extraordinary life. From internationally recognized fashions and handwritten letters to childhood treasures, jewelry, historic documents, and personal possessions—these remarkable objects tell the story of Diana as a daughter, sister, wife, mother, humanitarian, and global icon.

Exclusive to this stop on the tour, the Reagan Library adds to the international collection by pairing Princess Diana's artifacts with items from President and Mrs. Reagan’s archival collection. This one-of-a-kind pairing tells the story of the Princess of Wales and the enduring transatlantic bond between the U.S. and the U.K. It brings together iconic dresses and personal treasures from Princess Diana and Nancy Reagan, highlighting how each used their global platform to champion humanitarian work, shape fashion history, inspire millions, and leave a lasting influence on modern culture.

Displayed together for the very first time, this landmark exhibition also unveils previously unknown artifacts and items unique to the Reagan Library. This exhibition offers visitors an unprecedented opportunity to experience Diana's life, legacy, and enduring impact.

Link to join: tinyurl.com/IkeBookClub

IKE'S BOOK CLUB:﻿ ﻿A Yearlong Journey﻿

Join Ike's Book Club for a yearlong journey into the profound legacy and context of the 34th president. Our program features one book per quarter, each including a community Virtual Roundtable discussion and a special in-person Author Event.

Spring Quarter:

Ike’s Road Trip

by Dr. Brian C. Black

This book explores Dwight Eisenhower's participation in the 1919 Transcontinental Motor Convoy, which assessed the nation's roadways for military use and later served as inspiration for the Interstate Highway Act of 1956.

• Virtual Roundtable: Tuesday, 2/24 at 6 p.m.

• Author Event: Tuesday, 3/31 at 6 p.m.

Summer Quarter:

Rising Star, Setting Sun

by Mr. John T. Shaw

Detailing the complex transition of power from President Dwight D. Eisenhower to John F. Kennedy, this book examines the shift that symbolized a new generational era in American politics.

• Virtual Roundtable: Tuesday, 5/26 at 6 p.m.

• Author Event: Tuesday, 6/30 at 6 p.m.

Fall Quarter:

Whistle-Stop Politics

by Mr. Edward Segal

Take an entertaining journey through 185 years of American politics, exploring how campaigning by train profoundly shaped elections, journalism, and culture.

• Virtual Roundtable: Tuesday, 8/25 at 6 p.m.

• Author Event: Tuesday, 9/29 at 6 p.m.

Winter Quarter:

The Real Ike: Eisenhower Fact and Fiction

by Martin Mack Teasley

Drawing on experience as a former deputy director of the Eisenhower Presidential Library, the author presents a fresh perspective on "Ike," separating fact from fiction, addressing common myths, and answering frequently asked questions.

• Virtual Roundtable: Tuesday, 10/27 at 6 p.m.

• Author Event: Tuesday, 12/8 at 6 p.m.

Veterans Day book event explores the lasting imprint of war on those who serve and the families who love them.

Kathy Poulsen Romero, author of Letters from Heartbreak Ridge

In conversation with Matthew Algeo, author of Harry Truman’s Excellent Adventure and When Harry Met Pablo

For more than 70 years, a tattered box tied with a lace ribbon sat tucked away in the home of Kathy Poulsen Romero’s parents. Yellowed with age, its contents remained unopened until Romero finally discovered what had been hidden inside: more than 70 carefully preserved letters her father had written to her mother while serving in the Korean War.

The letters followed a young soldier from home to the front lines, including the brutal fighting at Heartbreak Ridge. They offered a firsthand account of a war that would shape a generation, but for Romero, their significance was far more personal. In the pages of those letters, she found the story of her parents’ courtship and glimpses of a father she had never fully known.

As she read, a different side of her father began to emerge—not simply the man she remembered, but the young soldier, devoted husband, and man behind the experiences that had shaped his life. What began as the discovery of a family treasure became an extraordinary journey toward understanding her parents and the lasting imprint of war on those who serve and the families who love them.

Both the concert band and book event are included with museum admission, which is free for Truman Library Institute members. Event registration is not required.

Open Admission Join us for a special Veterans Day concert featuring the AIRLIFTER BRASS, the Brass Quintet of the United States Air Force Band of Mid-America. With the traditional instrumentation of two trumpets, French horn, trombone, and tuba, the ensemble adds a percussionist to expand its versatility and showcase the outstanding musicianship of its members.

Each Airlifter Brass program is thoughtfully planned for a blend of inspiration and entertainment. Its repertoire has universal appeal and includes military marches, jazz standards, and patriotic favorites.

Whether performing for a head of state, before a capacity crowd in their 10-state touring area, or for troops at home or abroad, Airlifter Brass reflects the heritage and pride of our great nation and the United States Air Force. This tour holds special meaning for tubist SSgt Charles Hilton, for the opportunity to represent the Air Force in his native state Arkansas.

This program is presented by the Clinton Foundation and the Clinton Presidential Library in partnership with the MacArthur Museum of Arkansas Military History.
